directionInline.text: Core-Forge threshold is layered masonry and scarred ancient structure under ordinary modern construction, with no operator console in view. Theo, Rae and Adrian remain the foreground subjects; use doorways and wall seams to frame the three-way confrontation.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Theo, Rae and Adrian approach the Core-Forge through ordinary modern construction laid over ancient foundations. Some walls align impossibly with older ones, but the characters remain visually dominant.
Panel 2 — Theo recognizes Adrian's intent before any mechanism is shown: 'You brought us here to do it again.'
Panel 3 — Adrian: 'I brought you here because I don't know what else stops this.' Keep him frightened by his own conclusion rather than authoritative.
Panel 4 — Rae: 'Not knowing should terrify you.' Adrian: 'It does.' No one touches a console, studies a schematic or explains how the Reset works.

Panel 5 — Wide threshold panel. Rae stands centered a step ahead of Theo and Adrian; all three face the same scarred chamber entrance but keep visible distance from one another. Old dark masonry and newer construction meet around the doorway.
Panel 1 — Final ancient council in a plain neutral chamber. Everyone looks exhausted by years of knowing one another through war. Kyn enters without ceremony and takes an ordinary seat.
Panel 2 — Mero: 'Tell me what I'm missing.' Kyn: 'Sleep.' Let the answer land as bodily truth before philosophy.
Panel 3 — Mero presses. Kyn refuses the abstraction and begins with children waking afraid of battles they cannot see.

Panel 4 — Kyn continues through people hating strangers because of old marks and the living carrying the dead into the next room. Use specific remembered faces or gestures, not a cosmic empathy montage.
Panel 5 — Oryon: 'Then we end the threat before it reaches another room.' His answer comes from grief, not calculation.

Panel 6 — Arbiter: 'We have been ending threats for years.' Hold the whole exhausted council in a wide still panel: Kyn seated, Mero standing, Oryon rigid, Arbiter looking down at the table, with no one immediately answering.
Panel 1 — Present Theo walks the Core-Forge corridor. Match the composition with ancient Theo carrying papers through the same geometry on the next panel.
Panel 2 — Ancient Theo in the same stride and framing. No ghost overlay; this is one person's restored continuity shown through matched time.
Panel 3 — Present Theo: 'I know this hallway.' Present Rae: 'So do I.' Their recognition is mundane and bodily.
Panel 4 — Alternate ancient Rae waiting outside the familiar door with present Rae occupying the same position in modern construction.
Panel 5 — Theo: 'I hated that door.' Rae: 'I used to wait outside it.' End on the present pair realizing they remember habits and dislike, not just historic events.

directionInline.text: Wide exhausted council composition. Flux's established chair remains empty and clearly identifiable. Show only established participants; Regent is absent from the room and from background silhouettes.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Wide council composition with the established participants present as people who know one another. One familiar place associated with Flux remains empty; do not add an unidentified mystery figure.
Panel 2 — Afterlight: 'There isn't enough of me for what we've done.' Atlas: 'Then we stop doing it.' Their exchange starts from exhaustion and care.
Panel 3 — Starbreaker: 'And let the next catastrophe choose for us?' Redlin: 'We have chosen catastrophe often enough on our own.' Let old relationship history sharpen both lines.
Panel 4 — Oryon: 'Doing nothing is still a choice.' He is afraid of futures he has seen, not delivering doctrine.
Panel 5 — Arbiter: 'So is pretending this room can make one without blood on it.' The room has no clean moral high ground left.
Panel 6 — Kyn: 'Then stop asking for a clean choice.' End on the whole group in silence, with Flux's empty place still part of the human absence rather than a puzzle mechanism.

directionInline.text: Central scar chamber is a rough overlap of ancient and modern material: split floor, misaligned wall seams and worn surfaces, with no visible control station. Keep Rae spatially between Theo and Adrian as their positions separate across the chamber.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Central scar chamber. Ancient and modern material overlap, but there is no obvious device waiting to be operated. Adrian stands where he once made a choice.

Panel 2 — Adrian stands on an old worn floor mark facing the central scar: 'I can close it.' Theo steps between Adrian and the scar: 'You mean erase it.' Rae remains off to one side, watching both men claim the center of the room.
Panel 3 — Adrian: 'I mean stop this before people start killing for memories they received yesterday.' Keep his fear tied to the people seen in Issue 7.
Panel 4 — Theo: 'They were stolen from them.' Rae looks from Adrian to Theo, realizing both men are framing everyone else's memory as something they can administer.
Panel 5 — Rae: 'That doesn't make them yours to give back.' Theo: 'Whose are they?'

Panel 6 — Rae steps fully between Theo and Adrian and says, 'Theirs.' End in a medium frontal panel with Rae centered, Theo on one side, Adrian on the other, and the scar chamber pushed into the background.
Panel 1 — Outside the council door. Kyn and Afterlight sit somewhere unceremonious while muffled argument continues behind them. Let exhaustion soften faction distinctions.
Panel 2 — Kyn: 'If it stopped tonight, could they heal?' Afterlight answers, 'Some.'
Panel 3 — Kyn: 'That's all?' Afterlight: 'That's always all.' Their disappointment is shared rather than argumentative.
Panel 4 — Kyn: 'I keep wanting more than that.' Afterlight recognizes the same impossible desire in herself.

Panel 5 — Afterlight: 'So do I. That's how we hurt people.' End almost tenderly, with two people from opposing philosophies admitting that demanding complete repair can become another form of violence.
Panel 1 — Present Rae reaches a familiar threshold. Match her posture to ancient Rae seated beside Arbiter during the final council.
Panel 2 — Ancient Arbiter asks, 'If Mero authorizes it, will you record the decision?' Rae answers, 'Yes.' Her participation is ordinary and professional, which makes it harder to disown.
Panel 3 — Arbiter: 'You disagree.' Rae: 'I disagree with calling it mercy.' Keep them close enough to feel like longtime colleagues rather than abstract opponents.
Panel 4 — Arbiter: 'What would you call it?' Present Theo hears enough of the recovered exchange to understand Rae resisted the language without escaping the decision.
Panel 5 — Rae: 'Something we had no right to do and no courage left not to do.' End on present Rae carrying the same unresolved judgment; she was neither pure dissenter nor willing apologist.
Panel 1 — After the council, Mero and ancient Adrian remain alone in the plain room. No machine or schematic is present; the decision is already moral before it becomes an act.
Panel 2 — Mero: 'I need you to do it.' Adrian: 'No.' The refusal is immediate and personal.
Panel 3 — Mero: 'You know every road between them.' Adrian: 'I carried messages. I opened doors.' Show the burden of being the person who moved between all sides.

Panel 4 — Mero: 'You watched us use every door you opened to find another battlefield.' He gestures toward the open council-room door, then places the same hand against his own chest. Adrian remains still across from him.
Panel 5 — Adrian: 'That doesn't make this mine.' Mero steps closer but does not command him like a technician.

Panel 6 — Mero: 'Nothing about this belongs to one person. That's why I am asking the one who belonged to none of us.' End on Adrian alone in the foreground between two open doorways leading in opposite directions.
Panel 1 — Present Theo stands outside the same door where ancient Theo once waited. Past and present occupy matching compositions without labels.

Panel 2 — Ancient Mero sits heavily on the bench outside the familiar door: 'If they forgot us, could they become something else?' Junior Theo stands beside him with papers tucked under one arm and answers, 'Maybe,' without looking certain.
Panel 3 — Mero: 'That's more hope than I've heard all year.' Theo: 'It's not permission.' Keep Theo visibly junior but morally present.
Panel 4 — Mero: 'I know.' Theo: 'Do you?' The relationship allows the question to land harder than a speech.

Panel 5 — Return to present Theo. He remembers that he saw the possible freedom in forgetting and also warned that imposed forgetting would continue the war's coercion. End on responsibility without making him the architect of the Reset.

directionInline.text: Match ancient and present camera positions precisely: Adrian occupies the same floor mark and body angle in both times. Rae's hand physically stops Theo; her body then turns across the composition to stop Adrian. No control interface appears.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Ancient Adrian in the remembered Reset position, beginning the irreversible gesture under Mero's authority. Match directly to present Adrian occupying the same place.
Panel 2 — Present Theo moves toward the physical scar to force memory fully open while saying, 'Everyone should know what was taken.'
Panel 3 — Rae: 'Yes.' Theo: 'Then let me do this.' Rae: 'No.' She catches his hand before the repeated gesture completes.
Panel 4 — Match ancient Adrian continuing with present Adrian preparing to repeat his own old choice. Rae turns from Theo toward him.
Panel 5 — Adrian: 'Rae—' She cuts him off: 'You too.' The present composition now visibly diverges from the ancient one.
Panel 6 — Rae: 'Nobody chooses for everyone again.' End with both men stopped by a person refusing the premise that either forgetting or forced remembering can be imposed as a universal solution.
Panel 1 — After the choice not to repeat either coercive act, nothing spectacular resets. The chamber remains imperfectly overlapped and distant human voices continue outside.

Panel 2 — Theo looks back at the unchanged scar chamber: 'So what happens now?' Rae is already walking toward the exit and answers over her shoulder, 'People remember what they remember.' Nothing in the room changes around them.
Panel 3 — Adrian: 'And if it starts the war again?' He is asking from lived guilt, not seeking a new mechanism.
Panel 4 — Rae: 'Then we stop the war.' Adrian: 'That's not the same thing.'
Panel 5 — Rae: 'Exactly.' End on the trio leaving the place without repairing it. Conflict remains something people must address without controlling memory itself.

directionInline.text: Observation window with Theo, Rae and Adrian small against a normal star field containing one obvious dark absence where a familiar cluster should be. Keep the frame free of alarms, overlays, labels and instruments.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Quiet observation window after the immediate crisis. Theo, Rae and Adrian look at a familiar region of deep space. No alarms or instruments announce the problem.
Panel 2 — Theo notices first: 'Were those always gone?' Keep the missing stars as literal negative space rather than an effect.
Panel 3 — Rae: 'No.' She recognizes the absence with the same certainty that once accompanied impossible memories.
Panel 4 — Adrian: 'I don't know.' Give the admission room; for once he does not hide uncertainty behind protection or authority.
Panel 5 — Theo: 'You finally said it.' Adrian: 'Get used to hearing it.'

Panel 6 — Final wide panel: three small people facing a sky with a meaningful absence. Truth has returned unevenly; certainty has diminished. Do not reveal Flux, Regent or a technical explanation for the missing stars.
